issues.description: The problem statement/UML specifies acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity), but the provided solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (missing supplierName and ingredientName separation). This mismatch will confuse students about the required method signature and may break tests expecting the documented signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Align all artifacts on one signature. Prefer updating SealSaloon.acceptSupplyDelivery to accept (String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity) and use ingredientName for stock updates; supplierName can be ignored if not needed. Update any example calls accordingly.

issues.description: The problem statement/UML does not specify a Stock.setStockIngredients(...) method (and suggests adding getters for private fields), but both template and solution include a public setter that allows replacing the entire internal array. This contradicts the encapsulation guidance and can confuse students about the intended Stock API surface.
issues.suggestedFix: Remove setStockIngredients from Stock (or make it package-private and clearly mark it as testing-only). If needed for manual testing, keep it only in Main or provide controlled methods like addToStockIngredients/emptyStock per UML.

issues.description: The template Main (commented example) calls acceptSupplyDelivery("Bacon", 50, 100) with 3 arguments, which conflicts with the problem statement/UML requiring 4 arguments (supplier name + ingredient name + price + quantity). This creates confusion when students try to follow the provided example.
issues.suggestedFix: Update the Main example call to match the documented signature, e.g., acceptSupplyDelivery("CitySupplier", "Bacon", 50, 100), or adjust the problem statement if the intended signature is actually 3 parameters.

issues.description: The problem statement specifies acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity), but the solution implements acceptSupplyDelivery(String name, int price, int quantity) (missing the supplierName parameter and using a different parameter naming/arity). This breaks requirement-to-code mapping because students will look for a 4-parameter method matching the described API.
issues.suggestedFix: Change the method signature to match the statement: public static void acceptSupplyDelivery(String supplierName, String ingredientName, int price, int quantity), and use ingredientName internally (supplierName may be unused but should be present).

issues.description: The problem statement says SealSaloon has a final Stock stock attribute (read-only after construction), while also stating that the stock attribute must be static. The solution exposes it as static final Stock stock with a static getter, but the statement refers to it as an instance attribute named stock. This mixed instance-vs-static framing can confuse students about whether to access stock via instances or the class.
issues.suggestedFix: Align artifacts by clearly specifying 'static final Stock stock' in the problem statement (and in the diagram notes), and describe access as SealSaloon.getStock()/SealSaloon.stock rather than via an instance field.

issues.description: Main.java in both template and solution calls acceptSupplyDelivery with 3 parameters (ingredientName, price, quantity), while the problem statement specifies a 4-parameter version including supplier name. This inconsistency makes it unclear which API students should implement and test against.
issues.suggestedFix: Update Main.java examples to call acceptSupplyDelivery with 4 parameters (supplierName, ingredientName, price, quantity) to match the required signature, or adjust the problem statement to the 3-parameter signature if supplierName is not intended.
